# Governance

The Open Practice Framework is an open, community-correctable body of work. This page explains how decisions get made today and how that's meant to widen as more people take part.

## Who maintains it

The framework was started by Rob Hunter, who maintains it today. Maintaining it means reviewing proposals, keeping the component register accurate, and answering for what is published. It doesn't mean the framework belongs to one person's view of the practice. The [MIT License](../LICENSE) lets anyone use, adapt, and redistribute it.

## How decisions are made

- **Corrections** (something is wrong, out of date, or contradicts a cited source) are accepted on the evidence. They're kept visible and dated in the [change log](../CHANGELOG.md), not silently rewritten.
- **Changes to content** start as an issue or pull request. Anything larger than a wording fix should start as an issue, so the shape can be agreed before work is spent on it.
- **Changes to structure** (adding, renumbering, merging, or retiring a component) get an issue first, with the reason and the effect on links. Component identities stay stable because other people cite them.
- **When a proposal is declined**, the reason is written down in the thread. A decline is about fit for this implementation, not a verdict on the contributor's practice.
- **Disagreement is welcome.** If you think a decision was wrong, reopen it with new evidence or a clearer case.

## Widening maintenance

As people contribute steadily, the aim is to add maintainers with review rights for the parts they know well (for example, a technical method or Section 90). A new maintainer is proposed in a public issue, and the existing maintainers agree before access changes. The [CODEOWNERS](CODEOWNERS) file will record who reviews which paths.

## Forks and adaptations

Forking and adapting the framework for your own practice is the point. You don't need permission. If you share what you changed, through an [adaptation note](https://github.com/robhunter-labs/penetration-testing-practice-framework/issues/new?template=adaptation.yml), it helps the next team, even if the change never comes back here.

## Relationship to other guidance

The framework sits beside established testing and program guidance (OWASP, NIST, PTES, CREST, MITRE, and others). It doesn't claim their endorsement, and a mapping to any of them is a reading aid, not a statement that they've reviewed this work.

## Conduct

Everyone taking part follows the [code of conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
